p.i: siquidem M. D. LI. Hieronymum Bolsecum è cellis & pædore Monachorum excitavit, qui verissimam de Sanctorum Prædestinatione doctrinam, id est, certissimum salutis nostræ fundamentum evertere, & aperto Pelagianismo commutare conaretur. Sed erroris convictus urbe primum à vobis, deinde tota etiam vicina ditione extrusus est. Atque hic uti reliquo vitæ tempore incertis sedibus vagatur, ita certam animo religionem nullam tenet. Jam vero toties deiectus veritatis hostis præcipuum è suis ducibus & antesignanis tandem produxit. Anno enim M. D. LIII. ad vos horrendum illud & ex omni errorum colluvie conflatum monstrum Servetus venit: vel, ut ego potius sentio, Dominus ad justam nominis sui (quod impurus ille toties & ore & scriptis blasphemaverat) ultionem Servetum ad vos dignum de ipso supplicium sumpturos adduxit, cuius vel solo halitu Satan nocentissimum erroris venenum (per quod Domino nostro Jefu Christo sua veraque Deitas adimitur, id est, fidei nostræ basis convellitur) ita quibusdam afflavit, ut ne gravi quidem istius supplicio illi territi postea silerent, aut saniores essent. main_text.notes: The whole page is set in italic type, so the running text is marked as italic throughout. The first word "siquidem" is a fragment carried over from the previous page. The text ends with the printed hyphen of "hu-", which continues on the next page. The faint grey marks below the last line are show-through or stains and are left out. Note that the Latin "Iefu" is printed with a capital I and is rendered as "Jefu" under the i/j rule. "Seruetus" and "Servetus" are the same name in different letter forms; the printed form is "Seruetus" with u, and the i/j and u/v rule was applied to it. Where the printed page has a lowercase "s" long s, it has been written as plain s.
